common_name: Bee-You Bee-Happy Bee Balm (Compact Mildew-Resistant Modern Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Bee-Happy is a compact, mildew-resistant bee balm from the Dutch-bred Bee-You series, one of the newest bee balm introductions with strong disease resistance for a humid Gulf South summer.

directions: Plant in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade; Bee-Happy is a compact bee balm from the Bee-You series, bred with strong powdery mildew resistance that keeps its foliage looking healthy well into a humid Gulf South summer, when older bee balm varieties often defoliate badly. It bears the classic shaggy, tubular flowers over a tidy, well-branched mound that draws hummingbirds, bees, and butterflies through the summer bloom season. The compact size fits easily into a mixed perennial border without the sprawling habit of some heirloom Monarda types. Provide good air circulation with adequate spacing to further support disease resistance, and divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.
sources: AB Cultivars — US Plant Patent PP29080

common_name: Decadence Lemon Meringue Baptisia (Yellow False Indigo on Dark Stems)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun to light partial shade, choosing a permanent site since Baptisia develops a deep taproot and resents transplanting once established; Lemon Meringue is a compact Decadence-series hybrid bred by Hans Hansen with lemon-yellow flowers on striking charcoal-black stems.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun to light partial shade, choosing a permanent site since Baptisia develops a deep taproot and does not transplant well once established. Lemon Meringue is a compact Decadence-series hybrid bearing spikes of clear lemon-yellow, pea-like flowers held on dramatic near-black stems in late spring, followed by dark seedpods that provide fall and winter interest. Like other Baptisia it is extremely long-lived, drought-tolerant, and essentially maintenance-free once established, functioning almost like a small flowering shrub in the perennial border while also serving as a larval host plant for several butterfly species. Avoid dividing or transplanting mature plants; simply cut back in late winter if a tidier form is wanted.
sources: Proven Winners — US Plant Patent PP24280

common_name: Decadence Blueberry Sundae Baptisia (Compact Deep Indigo-Blue False Indigo)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun to light partial shade, choosing a permanent site since Baptisia develops a deep taproot and resents transplanting once established; Blueberry Sundae is a compact Decadence-series hybrid from Walters Gardens with deep indigo-blue flowers on an upright, tidy form.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun to light partial shade, choosing a permanent site since Baptisia develops a deep taproot and does not transplant well once established. Blueberry Sundae bears dense spikes of deep indigo-blue, pea-like flowers on a compact, upright plant, part of the Decadence series bred for more manageable garden size than the sprawling wild Baptisia species while keeping the genus's legendary toughness and longevity. Following bloom, dark seedpods provide fall and winter interest, and the plant serves as a larval host for several native butterfly species. It is extremely drought-tolerant and essentially maintenance-free once established, functioning almost like a small flowering shrub. Avoid dividing or transplanting mature plants; simply cut back in late winter if a tidier form is wanted.
sources: Walters Gardens — US Plant Patent PP23891

common_name: Glamour Girl Garden Phlox (Mildew-Resistant Coral-Pink Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, spacing generously for airflow; Glamour Girl is a Walters Gardens Garden Girls-series phlox bred for very good powdery mildew resistance, a major advantage over many older garden phlox in the humid Gulf South.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, spacing plants generously for good air circulation; Glamour Girl bears large, domed clusters of hot coral-pink flowers held on dark purple stems, part of the Garden Girls series bred for very good powdery mildew resistance, the fungal disease that disfigures the foliage of many older tall garden phlox varieties in humid summer conditions. Its more compact, tidy habit than heirloom phlox cultivars fits well into a mixed perennial border. Deadhead the central flower cluster once it fades to encourage side-shoot rebloom, and avoid overhead watering to further reduce disease pressure. In zone 9, tall phlox is treated as a somewhat short-lived perennial and may decline after a couple of seasons in intense summer heat, so division and replanting every few years helps maintain vigor.
sources: Walters Gardens — US Plant Patent PP25778

common_name: Volcano Purple with White Eye Garden Phlox (Highly Mildew-Tolerant Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, spacing generously for airflow; the Volcano series was bred from an Eastern European heirloom line noted for exceptional powdery mildew tolerance, a significant advantage for tall garden phlox in the humid Gulf South.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, spacing plants generously for good air circulation; this Volcano-series garden phlox produces richly fragrant purple flowers with a crisp white eye, held in dense trusses that can carry over a hundred blooms per stem at peak. The Volcano series was bred from a mildew-tolerant Eastern European heirloom line specifically to overcome the powdery mildew problems that plague many older tall phlox cultivars in hot, humid climates, making it a strong choice for a Gulf South perennial border. Deadhead the central flower cluster once it fades to encourage side-shoot rebloom, and avoid overhead watering to further support disease resistance. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.
